notes: Inspected all 10 current portable frames for the 115,282-triangle revision. The slender brick shaft, lower stone corbel crown, upper open belfry, exposed bell with curved iron support, lightning mast, clock and attached Cappella di Piazza retain the photographed silhouette and visible details.

The final chapel groin-vault surfaces meet the arch crowns without crossing the openings. Corner corbels connect diagonally into the tower; chapel cornice backing is continuous. Low relief frieze figures lie below the coping rather than standing on the roof. Niche figures, iron railings, drain spouts and the two-sided vane remain legible.

Inspected all 10 current shared sky-PMREM frames, including the north-up placement view. Brick and crown ashlar have metric joints, while the carved chapel uses neutral raw limestone without a second masonry grid. Iron bell supports and railings remain distinct from the stonework.

All four sides, distant silhouette and close chapel/crown/bell views were inspected. The geographic fixture loads the model, retains shared surfaces, and passes unloading assertions. The plan shows the attached chapel on the correct piazza-facing side and keeps the stone crown's overhang rather than stretching the narrow shaft.

The exact-QID tower outline 265416598 provides the anchor and axis. Independently mapped chapel 252463679 and city museum photographs fix native -Z toward Piazza del Campo, resolving the square tower's directional ambiguity. Anchor [11.332198478,43.318289062] and heading 0.918998496 radians are preserved in the current registered placement.

The north-up placement capture agrees with the mapped tower and chapel arrangement. Native dimensions retain the owner's approximately 7 m shaft and 102 m lightning-tip height. Terrain contact establishes the ground origin; minor courtyard and piazza paving differences remain host terrain details rather than a false absolute survey claim.

fidelityReview.notes: Finished detailed original exterior reconstruction based on Siena city and museum references, city tourism bell photographs, and the Campanologia dimensions. Included are the two distinct stone crowns, exposed bell with reconstructed curved iron support, mast and vane, shaft apertures and holes, clock, chapel arches and vault, cornice relief, figure niches, roof coping and railings. The city gives approximately 87 m masonry and 102 m lightning tip; the bell association gives 87.45 m masonry and an ambiguously scoped 97 m including bell structure. The curved frame apex is reconstructed at 91.1 m to match the primary aerial and known 2.34 m bell height, rather than stretching it to the ambiguous figure. Small sculptures, weathering and brick repairs use the project's original polygonal exterior style. The rest of Palazzo Pubblico and internal rooms remain separate.
